newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: New Ashanti mines on track for 1998 start.
newsitem.headline: New Ashanti mines on track for 1998 start.

text.p: Plans by Ghanaian gold mining giant Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd to bring on stream two West African gold mines in 1998 are unaffected by the recent nosedive in world prices, Ashanti said on Wednesday.
"Since they are being arranged by project finance they are on track," Ashanti corporate affairs manager James Anaman told Reuters. "Through our hedging policy we are okay for now."
Ashanti aims to produce 170,000 ounces a year over seven years at a cash cost of $225/ounce from a new mine at Bibiana in Ghana by investing $83 million, he said by telphone from Accra.
Production from its other new mine project at Siguiri in Guinea would produce 150,000 ounces/year at a cash cost of $220/ounce, requiring an investment of $55 million, he added.

World gold prices slid to 12-year lows last Thursday after Australia's central bank said it had sold 167 tonnes of its gold reserves over the past six months -- more than the annual Ghanaian production of around 51 tonnes a year.
Gold Fields Minerals Services has estimated West African producers' average cost to be $200-250/ounce against a world average of $262.
That would help West African producers like Ashanti to buck a trend, particularly in South Africa, towards deeper and more costly mining, bank analysts say.
Anaman said Ashanti could ride out the gold price trough.
"Bibiana in Ghana should be coming on line by the middle of next year...the other in Siguiri in Guinea is scheduled to come on line by the end of 1998," he said.

Combined projected annual production from Bibiana and Siguiri of 300,000 ounces of gold per year would boost Ashanti's overall output towards 1.4 million ounces by 2000, from 1.1 million in 1996, Anaman said.
Proven and provable reserves at Bibiana totalled 1.5 million ounces, compared to two million at Siguiri, he added.
Ashanti already has three mines in Ghana and one in Zimbabwe.
Ashanti's overall 1997 gold output would be 1.1 million ounces "give or take a few thousand ounces", Anaman said. "By the first half of 1998, that will creep up as Bibiana starts."
Ashanti's 35 exploration projects in 12 African coutries were at various levels of development, with its mine project at Geita in Tanzania the most advanced.

"That will be going into pre-feasibility studies towards the end of the year," Anaman added. He ranked Niger, Burkina Faso, Guinea and then Mali as the most promising countries in Ashanti's home territory of West Africa.

Operations would also continue in Senegal and Mali but Ashanti would not consider "for the time being" investing in neighbouring Ivory Coast, which is trying to encourage mining investment, he said. -- Abidjan newsroom, + 225 21 90 90
